structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, 3D-reconstructed surfaces of isotonic biconcave red blood cells have a mean curvature that varies substantially across the surface (not constant, as for a surface-tension equilibrium), and in hypotonic dilution the cells become near-spherical.
structured_output.pass_criterion: For at least 90% of segmented isotonic biconcave RBC surface meshes, the coefficient of variation of mean curvature H across the surface (area-weighted, excluding the rim 5% of area) is greater than 0.5, and the sign of H changes between dimple and rim in at least 90% of cells; AND matched hypotonic cells (about 200 mOsm/kg) have sphericity (36*pi*V^2/A^3) greater than 0.9 in at least 70% of cells versus less than 0.8 in isotonic cells.
structured_output.fail_criterion: If more than 25% of isotonic biconcave cell meshes have a mean-curvature coefficient of variation below 0.2 (near-constant H within mesh noise estimated from the sphere-like hypotonic cells), or if hypotonic cells do not reach sphericity above 0.9 in at least 70% of cases, the claim is not supported.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's "surface of equilibrium" under surface tension alone is a constant-mean-curvature surface (Plateau/Delaunay surfaces) via the Young-Laplace equation with uniform pressure difference. This maps to the per-vertex mean curvature H of a reconstructed cell-membrane mesh. His "diluted blood" maps to hypotonic buffer. His non-surface-tension forces (osmotic inequilibrium, fluid crystal forces) are not tested here; only the necessary condition (non-constant H) and the sphere-in-hypotonic observation are. Modern caveat: red cell shape is governed by membrane bending elasticity and the spectrin cytoskeleton (Helfrich model), not an ideal fluid drop, so the test checks only Thompson's negative claim. No suitable public dataset was found.
structured_output.no_dataset_reason: I could not find a public dataset of 3D red blood cell surface reconstructions (holotomography, confocal or scanning-probe) with matched isotonic and hypotonic conditions and a verifiable landing page. A Zenodo API search for red blood cell tomography returned ten records and none had RBC 3D shape data. The nearest records were tomographic phase microscopy of other cell types (e.g. 10.5281/zenodo.7326417), red cell ektacytometry indices (10.5281/zenodo.5832570), and a SciDraw drawing (10.5281/zenodo.10118509). I did not confirm that any of these fits, and I will not guess an identifier for a dataset I could not verify. The papers arXiv 2409.20013 and 1404.2968 describe isotonic and hypotonic RBC 3D reconstructions, but I found no deposited data for them.
